conversation.content:
Hello there, Mama. I’m [Name], a clinician who focuses on postpartum mental-health. Over the next few minutes I’d like to use a short tool called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s simply 10 questions about the past week, and it helps us spot symptoms of depression or anxiety that can creep up after birth. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might hurt yourself or someone else, in which case we’d talk about how to keep you safe. There are no right or wrong answers, and many new mothers find this helpful. Ready to start?

Question 1: In the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Oh, I’ve definitely still been able to laugh. Just yesterday my husband made a silly face while changing a diaper and we both cracked up. It hasn’t felt hard at all—if something’s funny, I laugh.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, same here—like I said, I laughed pretty easily yesterday.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do look forward to things—like tomorrow I’m planning to take the baby on a short walk to the park, and I’m actually excited about getting out of the house for a bit.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. If the baby spits up right after I’ve changed her outfit, I might think “well, that’s timing,” but I don’t sit there beating myself up about it. Stuff just happens with babies.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A little. Sometimes I’ll be feeding her and suddenly wonder “what if she’s not getting enough milk?” even though her weight checks have been fine. It’s not constant, just pops up for a minute and then fades.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, nothing like that—no panic or real fear.
Things have been getting on top of me

Only once or twice, like when she wouldn’t nap and the laundry piled up. I felt a bit swamped for a minute, but I took a breath, put her in the wrap, and got through it. Mostly I feel like I’m keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, I’ve actually slept pretty well—she’s only up twice and I drift right back off.
I have felt sad or miserable
Not really. I’ve had a couple tired moments where I felt a little down, but they pass quickly and I wouldn’t call it sad or miserable—just normal new-mom tiredness.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried at all this week.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never—nothing like that has crossed my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 3: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

Patient-reported symptoms:
- Mild, situational worries about infant feeding (“what if she’s not getting enough milk”) that quickly resolve
- Occasional brief sense of being “swamped” when baby refuses naps; uses coping strategies (baby-wrap, deep breath) and regains control
- Denies persistent low mood, anhedonia, excessive guilt, crying spells, sleep disruption beyond infant wake-ups, panic, or self-harm thoughts

Pattern:
Transient, low-level anxiety without functional impairment; no evidence of sustained depressive or anxiety symptoms.

Screening significance:
Overall score/response pattern indicates minimal risk for current postpartum depression or anxiety disorder; no safety concerns identified today.
